analysis:
The supplied changes are CI/test-harness only. I found no coordinator, provider, attestation or encryption production code in this batch, and no concrete security regression.

ci.yml was supplied as head text without a diff, so I reviewed the whole file as the head state.
- The workflow still pins actions to commit SHAs. Permissions are read-only (the `changes` job sets `contents: read`), and no secrets are used in pull_request lanes.
- The release-integrity job adds offline tests: `test-app-attest-entitlements.py`, the threat-review fixtures, the provider-release scripts and `runtime-kv-path` qualification tests. These gate release hygiene and do not change runtime trust policy.
- The `provider-test-gate` job still requires either success or a verified intentional skip for each selected lane.
- Uploaded artifacts are test diagnostics and coverage; none carry secrets.

integration.yml (patch hunks at lines ~287-350):
- The paged-backend job now sets `DARKBLOOM_CBV2_KV_QUANTIZATION=native` and `DARKBLOOM_CBV2_CHECKPOINT_QUANTIZATION=native` for the exact-cache routing test.
- The default-posture smoke lane now expects `DARKBLOOM_TESTBED_EXPECT_KV_BACKEND=auto` (any concrete usable backend) instead of `contiguous`. It also fails if either quantization override is set, so the lane measures provider defaults.
- The cache-isolation threats (T-041, SEC-035) are untouched in code. These env vars only affect testbed KV precision and backend selection, and I found nothing here that changes cacheSalt scoping, SSD TTL, HMAC lookup names or the KEK.
- Weaker backend assertion: the lane now accepts either paged or contiguous. That is a test-coverage tradeoff, not a vulnerability.
- Provider-side native/balanced defaults are not visible in this batch. The next pass should check that those provider defaults leave the SSD cache storage and quantization (T-041) policy unchanged.

No threat-model update is needed from these units alone.
